fields.why: The outcome variable itself (age at introduction) is summarized as a mean: 'the mean age at introduction of complementary foods was 5.7 months'. A even listed it under primary_measures but did not list continuous.

The 'other' entry is the survey's hot-deck and sequential regression imputation of missing race/FPL, which is data preparation done by the survey. The brief lists data cleaning, but not imputation, as a non-procedure; a rule saying 'imputation is data handling, not a procedure' would decide it.
Subgroup prevalences are only set side by side with significance (25.2% vs 13.8% and others); no difference or ratio is computed. The only percentage-point figure is the 1.2-point sensitivity result.

brief_issues: Survey-supplied imputation (hot-deck and sequential regression) is not covered by the procedures or non-procedures lists.
